title: Kedoshim: holiness for everyone (Leviticus 19:2)
hookLine: holiness is spoken to the whole congregation, not only to priests

cards: For long stretches of Leviticus, holiness has had a dress code: linen garments, a golden plate, a turban. It's had an address: the sanctuary, the altar, the room behind the curtain.
And much of the time it's had a small cast: Aaron and his sons. The call to be holy was heard once already, back in chapter eleven, about food.
Still, a shepherd or a weaver listening might wonder whether holiness was mostly the priests' business. Then chapter nineteen opens, and it is spoken to everyone.

teach.b: In the 1917 Jewish Publication Society translation: "Speak unto all the congregation of the children of Israel, and say unto them: Ye shall be holy; for I the LORD your God am holy." All the congregation. Not the priests.
Everyone. The portion takes its name from that call: Kedoshim, holy ones.
Rashi, drawing on an older midrash, says this chapter was taught with the whole people gathered together, because most of the essentials of the Torah depend on it.
And read on: the chapter doesn't send anyone to the altar. Revere your mother and your father. Keep the Sabbath.
Don't steal, don't lie to each other. Pay a hired worker the same day; don't keep his wages overnight.
Rise before the gray head and honor the old. Keep honest scales and honest weights. Holiness, in Kedoshim, sits in a paycheck, a grocery scale, a seat given up on the bus.
The chapter switches back and forth between what we'd call ritual and what we'd call ethics, sometimes verse to verse, and never marks the difference.
Some teachers read that as the point: the holy and the decent aren't two departments. Over the next days, I'll take a few of these verses one at a time.
For today, just the opening: the call is to everyone, and it lands in ordinary places.

how: Kedoshim is read in synagogue in the spring, often together with Acharei Mot, and Leviticus 19 is often taught in Jewish ethics.

games.q: you're a hired laborer in the camp. you finish a day's work at sunset. when does Leviticus 19 say you get paid?
o: at the end of the week.
that same day, not kept overnight.
games.why: the wages shall not stay with the employer all night until morning. holiness, in Kedoshim, includes the paycheck.

practice: Pick something completely ordinary from your day: paying someone, answering an email, giving change at the register, cooking dinner.
Picture doing it as though it were part of a holy day: careful, honest, on time, with attention to the person on the other end. Not slower, necessarily; just set apart.

wordCard.voice: Kedoshim. Holy ones: the portion that calls the whole people to holiness, and finds it in wages, scales and honoring the old.

orig.note: Hebrew: "you shall be holy" (Leviticus 19:2), the words that name the portion.
